title: Nine Miles of Numbering
subtitle: 历史古迹 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 历史古迹（历史社会与文化·历史事件与人物）
meta: 主题语境：历史古迹（历史社会与文化·历史事件与人物）　|　核心词汇：century　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 century 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1901 my mother was asked to number ① century she could not finish, and she said the numbering was the whole of the lesson. The ② century, meaning the hundred years and not the ruins, was nine miles of wall and was numbered by whoever came last; century, she said, is the only thing in a record that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ century in that record had the same name, and the ④ century at the end, meaning the one the keepers kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever numbered properly. Century, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ century was the whole of the ruin, meaning the age it carried and not the hundred years. The ⑥ century, meaning the age and not any of that, is the only thing in a ruin that everybody visits and nobody questions; century, he said, is either something you number or the only word that means both a hundred years and an age. She said the age is the part they remember.

By 1908 the ⑦ century had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the wall. The ⑧ century of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine miles and eleven years of numbering; century, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ century I remember is the one at the end, which was numbered in 1913 and is still described as the oldest in the county. A ⑩ century, my grandmother said in 1918, is the only thing that improves by being numbered; every century, she said, is an age that has agreed to look like a hundred years. She said the age was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 世纪（指那一百年本身，与那些遗迹相对）
C. 固定搭配：number a century 给一个世纪编号
D. n. 世纪（指记录里每一个）
E. n. 世纪（指末尾那一个）
F. n. 年代（抽象：它承载的那份年岁）
G. n. 那份年岁（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The century, meaning the hundred years and not the ruins
century was the whole of the ruin
the century had become a number in a report
The century of the whole thing
A century, my grandmother said in 1918

answers.why: number a century 意为“给一个世纪编号”，1901 年母亲被要求给她读不完的那个世纪编号。
century 意为“世纪、百年”，指那一百年本身而不是那些遗迹，是九英里长的墙，由最后来的人编号。
century 指记录里每一个世纪，每一个都是同样的名字。
century 指末尾那一个（保管人保留的那一个），是唯一有人认真编号过的。
century 意为“年代”，抽象指它承载的那份年岁，父亲说 century 就是那片遗迹的全部。
century 为抽象用法，指那份年岁本身，是一片遗迹里人人都来参观、却没人质疑的东西。
century 意为“世纪、百年”，到 1908 年这个 century 成了报告里的一个数字。
century 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九英里和十一年的编号。
century 意为“世纪”，我记得的是末尾那一个，1913 年编过号，至今仍被说成全县最古老的。
century 为抽象总称，祖母说一个世纪是唯一会因为被认真编号而变好的东西。
